lessons.title: Sink or Float? The Prediction Game
lessons.focus: Predict then test twenty local objects (nail, coin, maize cob, charcoal, bottle top, mango seed, stone, leaf, wax, wire); tabulate surprises.
lessons.advanced: From the class table, state the rule that beats 'heavy things sink' with three counter-examples.

lessons.title: Density Decides: Wood, Stone and Steel
lessons.focus: Average density vs water (1000 kg/m³) predicts floating; the steel nail sinks but the steel sufuria floats — shape matters.
lessons.advanced: A hollow steel ball's average density is 600 kg/m³: what fraction of its volume is air?

lessons.title: Upthrust: Water Pushes Back
lessons.focus: Weigh a stone in air, then in water: apparent weight drops; upthrust measured with a spring balance.
lessons.advanced: Stone: 2.5 N in air, 1.5 N in water: upthrust, displaced water weight, and the stone's volume.

lessons.title: Archimedes' Principle
lessons.focus: Upthrust equals weight of displaced fluid; verify by collecting overflow from the eureka can and weighing it.
lessons.advanced: Show a floating object's displaced weight equals its own weight — derive the floating condition.

lessons.title: The Eureka Can Lab: Volume by Overflow
lessons.focus: Measure irregular volumes precisely by overflow; link displacement to Unit 1 density measurements.
lessons.advanced: An object displaces 120 mL and weighs 3.0 N in air: density, and will it float?

lessons.title: Why Ships Float: Shape Beats Material
lessons.focus: Same clay ball sinks, same clay as a bowl floats; average density includes the hollow; dhow and ferry examples.
lessons.advanced: Compute the minimum hollow fraction for a steel hull (ρ=7800) to float; why do ships sink when swamped?

lessons.title: Clay Boat Challenge I: Design for Cargo
lessons.focus: Design a clay hull to carry bottle-top cargo; predict capacity from displaced volume.
lessons.advanced: Boat clay mass 200 g; hull displaces 800 cm³ at gunwale: maximum safe cargo in grams?

lessons.title: Clay Boat Challenge II: Load Test and Stability
lessons.focus: Load to sinking; record capacity; stability: wide beams vs tall cargo; freeboard concept.
lessons.advanced: Explain via centre of gravity vs centre of buoyancy why top-heavy boats capsize.

lessons.title: The Hydrometer: A Floater That Measures
lessons.focus: Floating depth reveals density; milk purity testing at the dairy; battery acid testers; salinity for fish farmers.
lessons.advanced: Why does the hydrometer sink deeper in less-dense liquid? Derive the depth-density relation for a uniform stick.
